exposure: Essential Steps in Managing Obstetric Emergencies (ESMOE) structured training programme
outcome: Capacity of healthcare facilities to provide basic emergency obstetric and neonatal care signal functions (7 functions)
Capacity of healthcare facilities to provide comprehensive emergency care signal functions (9 functions)
cohort: The study involved healthcare professionals (doctors, advanced midwives, professional nurses) involved in maternity care, across 51 community health centres and 62 district hospitals in South Africa.
finding: The ESMOE training programme significantly improved the knowledge and skills of doctors, advanced midwives, and professional nurses, leading to a modest improvement in the functionality of healthcare facilities to provide emergency obstetric care.
